title: VPC & On‑Prem Operator Circuit‑Breaker Contingency Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This playbook defines operator-level circuit-breaker and contingency patterns for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem control planes). It collates policy thresholds, detection signals, automated mitigations, manual operator procedures, safe rollback/upgrade checkpoints, and evidence collection required for regulated customers. Use this document during incidents, preflight drills, and major upgrades.

Context and goals
- Scope: applies to control plane and runtime interactions that affect tenant request routing, model swap, KV cache integrity, and telemetry export for private deployments.
- Goals: preserve customer SLAs where possible, avoid data exposure, ensure safe rollback paths, and provide operator playbooks for predictable recovery.
- Assumptions: operators have access to the operator console, runbooks CLI, and emergency KMS keys.

Key failure classes and mapped circuit‑breaker patterns
1) Control‑plane congestion (eg. control plane queuing > 300ms median for 5m window).
   - Circuit: backpressure at ingress + degraded routing to local model variant.
   - Immediate operator action: enable ingress soft‑throttle and apply tenant‑level rate cap.
2) KV cache corruption or divergence (detection via checksum drift or replay failure).
   - Circuit: isolate affected tenant KV shards and switch to read‑through mode from immutable snapshot.
   - Immediate operator action: place affected tenants in read‑only mode and notify CS.
3) Model variant regression (quality monitor triggers > 2 regressions on golden prompts).
   - Circuit: automatic fallback to previous pinned model version; disable new quantized variant.
   - Immediate operator action: run evaluation harness and promote safe candidate if validated.
4) Telemetry egress failure (export failure rate > 10% for 3m).
   - Circuit: buffer telemetry locally and downgrade retention tier; raise incident with telemetry SRE.
   - Immediate operator action: increase buffer capacity and verify disk pressure.

SLO & trigger matrix (operators reference)
- Table: Event | Metric | Threshold | Prescribed action | Escalation
- Control plane latency | p50 > 200ms, p95 > 600ms | 5m sustained | soft throttle tenants; route to regional fallback | oncall-sre
- KV checksum drift | per-tenant checksum mismatch ratio > 0.5% | instant alert | isolate shard, enable read‑through | storage team
- Model quality | eval regression count >= 2 | rolling 10-run window | auto-fallback, run eval-runbook | applied-ml team
- Telemetry egress | export error rate >= 10% | 3m window | buffer & sample down telemetry | infra-observability

Circuit‑breaker implementation patterns
- Passive breakers: detection via Prometheus alerts + operator approvals (default for high‑risk fallbacks).
- Active breakers: operators can flip a breaker via the operator API to force routing changes, KV isolation, or model pinning. Use active breakers sparingly and only with documented evidence.

Operator API examples
1) Soft throttle a tenant (CLI example):
```
redwood-ops tenant-throttle --tenant-id tenant-123 --rate 10rps --duration 15m --reason "control-plane-latency-2027-01-12"
```
2) Isolate KV shard: (returns operation ID, watchable)
```
redwood-ops kv isolate --shard-id shard-42 --mode read-through --snapshot-id snap-20270111
```
3) Flip circuit for model fallback:
```
redwood-ops circuit flip --name model-fallback-tenant-123 --action enable --target-version v1.7.9
```

Evidence collection checklist (for regulated customers)
- Required artifacts: operation IDs, start/end timestamps, Prometheus alert IDs, sampled request traces (redacted PII), KV snapshot checksums, and signed operator approval record.
- Storage location: evidence bundles must be uploaded to the tenant evidence bucket under path: s3://evidence-prod/{tenant}/{incident-id}/. Ensure customer‑facing export uses the evidence export tool that redacts secrets.

Step‑by‑step contingency runbook (operator play sequence)
1) Triage (5 minutes)
   - Confirm alert: cross‑check Prometheus alert and the operator console incident view.
   - Document primary metric and affected tenants.
   - If multiple independent P0s present, escalate to incident lead.
2) Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - Apply passive mitigation: increase soft‑throttles, enable caching fallbacks.
   - If containment fails, activate circuit via operator API (record reason and approval).
3) Stabilize (30–120 minutes)
   - Validate service health and reduce routing diversity to known good variants.
   - Run targeted smoke tests (see Smoke Test commands below).
4) Restore & evidence (120+ minutes)
   - If safe, progressively remove circuit actions in reverse order.
   - Assemble evidence bundle and notify customer success with the incident summary template.

Smoke test commands and expected outputs
- Lightweight generation smoke test (10 requests):
```
redwood-ops smoke test --endpoint /v1/predict --retries 1 --count 10 --sample-prompts smoke-basic.json
```
Expected: 10/10 responses under 250ms median, no error status > 5%.

Safe rollback and upgrade checkpoints
- Define safepoints before any upgrade or model swap: snapshot KV metadata, freeze scheduling windows for 15 minutes pre‑upgrade, and create an immutable artifact manifest.
- Upgrade workflow (high level):
  1) Create safety snapshot: redwood-ops snapshot create --scope cluster --tag preupgrade-{timestamp}
  2) Canary: rollout to <1% of traffic per tenant and run 250 synthetic queries.
  3) Evaluate: run eval harness and watch metric deck for 30m.
  4) Promote or rollback: use the operator circuit to pin previous artifact if quality or latency regressions hit thresholds.
- Rollback considerations: ensure no schema migrations were applied that prevent rollbacks; if stateful, execute orchestrated state backfill after rollback.

Communication & escalation templates
- Internal slack notify snippet: 
"[INCIDENT] {short_title} — Impact: {tenants} — Action: {action} — ETA rollback {eta} — Owner: {owner}"
- Customer facing: include a short timeline, what we changed, mitigation steps, and next steps. Attach the evidence bundle link and recommended post‑incident actions for the customer.

Drill & validation schedule
- Quarterly drills: one full canary failure simulation (including KV corruption simulation) and one telemetry outage simulation.
- Acceptance criteria for drills: operator completes containment and restore within documented SLOs and produces an evidence bundle.

Runbook ownership and change process
- Owners: eng-private-deployments oncall rotation (primary), eng-sre (secondary).
- Changing this playbook: propose ADR to eng-private-deployments/design-review then schedule a drill to validate changes before publishing.

Appendices
A) Common operator error codes and how to act
- ERR-KV-CHK-01: checksum mismatch — isolate and snapshot.
- ERR-CPL-THR-02: control plane throttled — investigate request hot keys.
B) Minimal config samples (YAML)
```
operator_circuit:
  name: model-fallback
  actions:
    - type: pin_model
      target: v1.7.9
    - type: throttle
      rate: 10rps
      duration: 15m
  approvals_required: 2
```
